items.name: Exotic smooth hermitian O_F-divisible groups (Definition 2.1, Remarks 2.2, 2.9)
items.statement: E/F ramified quadratic, p odd, uniformizer u with u^c = −u, n = 2r. Exo_{(n−1,1)}(S): (X, ι_X, λ_X) with X an O_F-divisible group of dimension n and height 2n, ι_X : O_E → End(X) satisfying the Kottwitz condition charpoly(ι_X(u) | Lie X) = (T − u)^{n−1}(T + u), the wedge condition ∧²(ι_X(u) − u | Lie X) = 0 and the spin condition (ι_X(u) ≠ 0 on Lie X_s at every geometric point), and λ_X a ι_X-compatible polarization with ker λ_X = X[ι_X(u)]; Exo^b the supersingular ones. Equivalently λ_X = σ_X ∘ ι_X(u) for a unique ι_X-compatible symmetrization σ_X. Exo_{(n,0)}(S): ι_X(u) − u kills Lie X.
items.locator: Definition 2.1, Remark 2.2, pp.8–9; Remark 2.9, p.10, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.4 (the relative Rapoport–Zink space N)
items.statement: For a fixed (𝐗, ι, λ) ∈ Exo^b_{(n−1,1)}(k̄), the functor N of quadruples (X, ι_X, λ_X; ρ_X) with ρ_X a quasi-morphism to the framing object on the special fibre (Definition 2.3) is a separated formal scheme, formally smooth of relative dimension n − 1 over Spf O_Ĕ, with two connected components [RZ96; RSZ17, Prop. 3.10; Wu, Thm. 5.18(2)].
items.locator: Definition 2.3 and Lemma 2.4, p.9, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The hermitian space 𝐕 of special quasi-homomorphisms (ramified case)
items.statement: With (X_0, ι_{X_0}, λ_{X_0}) supersingular of dimension 1 and height 2 over O_Ĕ, 𝐕 = Hom_{O_E}(X_0 ⊗ k̄, 𝐗) ⊗ Q, with (x, y)_𝐕 = u^{−2}λ_{X_0}^{−1} ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ_𝐗 ∘ x ∈ End_{O_E}(X_0) ⊗ Q ≅ E (2.1); it is nondegenerate and nonsplit of dimension n [RSZ17, Lemma 3.5]. The factor u^{−2} makes N(x) nonempty iff (x, x)_𝐕 ∈ O_F (footnote 9).
items.locator: §2.1, (2.1), p.10 and footnote 9, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.name: Absolute exotic p-divisible groups Exo^Φ (Definition 2.59, Remark 2.67)
items.statement: For F/Q_p unramified of degree f (q = p^f) and a partial CM type Φ ∋ φ_0 with Hom(E, Ĕ) = Φ ⊔ Φ^c: Exo^Φ_{(n−1,1)}(S) consists of p-divisible groups X of dimension nf and height 2nf with O_E-action satisfying the Kottwitz, wedge and spin conditions on Lie_{ψ_0}(X), the banal condition (O_E acts on Lie_{ψ_i}(X) via φ_i for 1 ≤ i ≤ f − 1), and a ι_X-compatible polarization with ker λ_X = X[ι_X(u)]; similarly Exo^Φ_{(n,0)}.
items.locator: Definition 2.59, p.37; Remark 2.67, p.42, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.statement: Using displays and O_F-displays [Zin02; Lau08; ACZ16]: with ε_i ∈ W(O_F)^× given by ^Vε_i = [ψ_i(u²)] − ψ̂_i(u²) and a unit μ_u with ^{F^f}μ_u/μ_u = Π_{i=1}^{f−1} ^{F^{f−1−i}}ε_i (2.21), the construction (P_0, Q_0, F′_{f−1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ F′_1 ∘ F_0, …) with pairing μ_u( , )_0 gives a morphism of prestacks −^rel : Exo^{Φ,b}_{(n−1,1)} → Exo^b_{(n−1,1)} on Sch^v_{/O_Ĕ} (2.22), which is an isomorphism. (Lemma 2.60: for 1 ≤ i ≤ f − 1, Q_i = (u ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ [φ_i(u)])P_i + I(R)P_i and F′_i is a Frobenius-linear isomorphism; Lemma 2.63: the kernel of F^♮ is Q^★ and endomorphisms preserving Q descend.)

items.name: Definition 1.1 (V♥_F) and admissible CM types
items.statement: V♥_F ⊆ V^spl_F ∪ V^int_F consists of v such that for every v′ ∈ V_F^(p) ∩ V^ram_F (p below v), the subfield of F̄_v generated by F_v and the Galois closure of E_{v′} is unramified over F_v; its complement in V^spl ∪ V^int is finite, and it is everything when E is Galois, contains an imaginary quadratic field, or V^ram_F = ∅ (Remark 1.2). For u ∉ V♥ … a CM type Φ is admissible (Notation 4.19) when Φ_v induces one place above split v, is pulled back from the maximal unramified subfield at inert v, and has reflex field unramified over E_u at ramified v.
items.locator: Definition 1.1 and Remark 1.2, p.3; Notation 4.19, p.56, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The auxiliary CM moduli Y and X′_L
items.statement: T_0 = {a ∈ E ⊗ R : Nm_{E/F}a ∈ R^×}; for a CM type Φ ∋ ι and level L_0, the PEL moduli Y of CM abelian varieties of type Φ is smooth projective of dimension 0 over E′ [Kot92], X′_L := X_L ⊗_E Y; its integral model Y over O_K (unitary O_E-abelian schemes of signature Φ with p-principal polarization and L_0^p-level) is finite étale over O_K [How12, Prop. 3.1.2].
items.locator: Notations 4.18–4.19, pp.56–57, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.name: Integral models X_m with Drinfeld level at a split place
items.statement: For u ∈ V♥_F split with V_F^(p) ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F: the moduli X_m over O_K of tuples (A_0, …; A, ι_A, λ_A, η^p_A, {η_{A,v}}, η_{A,u,m}) (signature nΦ − ι_w + ι_w^c, kernel conditions q_v^{1−ε_v} at v ∉ V^ram, Lie(A[u^{c,∞}]) of rank 1 via ι_w^c, the exotic (n, 0) condition at ramified v | p, and a Drinfeld level-m structure at u) is regular, flat (smooth for m = 0) and projective over O_K, with X_m ⊗ K ≅ X′_{L^u_{,m}L^u} ⊗ K [RSZ20, Thm. 4.5]; S^{R ∪ V_F^(p)} acts by étale correspondences.
items.locator: §4.3, pp.57–58 and footnotes 18–19, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.name: Integral models X_L̃ at a ramified place (exotic good reduction)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^ram_E with V_F^(p) ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F: the moduli X_L̃ of tuples with the exotic (n, 0) condition at ramified v ≠ u in U and the exotic (n − 1, 1) condition (Definition 2.59) at u forms a projective system of smooth projective schemes over O_K with finite étale transition maps and generic fibre X′_L̃ ⊗ K [RSZ20, Thm. 4.7, AT type (2)].

items.name: Proposition 4.30, first part (uniformization by the relative Rapoport–Zink space)
items.statement: For P_0 ∈ Y(O_K̆), X = lim X_L̃, X_0 the fibre over P_0 and X^∧_0 its completion along the locus where A[u^∞] is supersingular: with 𝐕 = Hom_{O_E}(A_0 ⊗ F̄_p, 𝐀) ⊗ Q (totally positive definite, nonsplit at u, with prescribed local lattices 𝚲_v, v ∈ U), the morphism Υ^rel : X^∧_0 → U(𝐕)(F)\[N × U(𝐕)(A^{∞,u}_F)/Π_{v∈U} 𝐋_v] (4.8), built from N^{Φ_u} and Corollary 2.65, is an isomorphism (as in [RZ96, Thm. 6.30]).
items.locator: §4.5, (4.8) and Proposition 4.30, pp.65–67, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.name: Special divisors N(x) and intersection numbers Int(𝐋) (Definitions 2.5–2.6)
items.statement: For 0 ≠ x ∈ 𝐕, N(x) is the maximal closed formal subscheme over which ρ_X^{−1} ∘ x lifts to a homomorphism X_0 ⊗ S → X; for X ⊆ 𝐕 with ⟨X⟩ finitely generated, N(X) = ⋂_{x∈X} N(x), depending only on ⟨X⟩ and proper when ⟨X⟩ is a lattice (Remark 2.26). For an O_E-lattice 𝐋 with basis x_1, …, x_n, Int(𝐋) := χ(O_{N(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{N(x_n)}), independent of the basis by Corollary 2.35.
items.locator: Definitions 2.5–2.6, p.10; §2.3 and Remark 2.26, p.21, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Theorem 2.7 (Kudla–Rapoport formula for exotic smooth Rapoport–Zink spaces)
items.statement: For E/F ramified with p odd, n = 2r even and 𝐕 nonsplit: for every O_E-lattice 𝐋 of 𝐕, Int(𝐋) = ∂Den(𝐋). Proof as in [LZa]: for L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕), the difference Φ_{L^♭} = ∂Den^v_{L^♭} − Int^v_{L^♭} is compactly supported, L^♭-invariant, with Fourier support in 𝐕^int; induction on val(L^♭) with Lemma 2.58 confines its support to S_{L^♭}, and a Fourier argument (non-special case) or the uncertainty principle [LZa, Prop. 8.1.6] (special case) kills it.
items.locator: Theorem 2.7, p.10; proof §2.7, pp.33–36, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 2.8 (the set ♭(𝐕))
items.statement: ♭(𝐕) is the set of hermitian O_E-modules in 𝐕 of rank n − 1; for L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕), V_{L^♭} = L^♭ ⊗ F and V^⊥_{L^♭} its orthogonal complement (V_{L^♭} is nondegenerate by the definition of hermitian O_E-module).
items.locator: Definition 2.8, p.10, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Remark 2.18 (local densities as Whittaker functions, ramified case)
items.statement: For T ∈ GL_n(E) representing 𝐋: W_T(s, 1_{4r}, 1_{H_r^{2r}}) = Den(H_{r+s}, 𝐋) for integers s ≥ 0 [KR14, Prop. 10.1, with L_{r,r} replaced by H_r (footnote 10)], hence log q·∂Den(𝐋) = W′_T(0, 1_{4r}, 1_{H_r^{2r}})/Π_{i=1}^r(1 − q^{−2i}).
items.locator: Remark 2.18 and footnote 10, pp.13–14, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 2.20 and Remark 2.21 (horizontal and vertical analytic parts)
items.statement: For L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕) and x ∈ 𝐕 \ V_{L^♭}: ∂Den_{L^♭}(x) = ∂Den(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩); ∂Den^h_{L^♭}(x) = 2 Σ_{L^♭ ⊆ L ⊆ L^∨, t(L ∩ V_{L^♭}) = 1} 1_L(x); ∂Den^v_{L^♭} = ∂Den_{L^♭} − ∂Den^h_{L^♭}. All three vanish off a compact C_{L^♭} and are locally constant on C_{L^♭} \ V_{L^♭}; if t(L ∩ V_{L^♭}) = 1 then t(L) = 2; and ∂Den^v_{L^♭}(x) = 2 Σ_{t(L ∩ V_{L^♭}) > 1} μ(t(L))1_L(x) with μ(t) = Π_{i=1}^{t/2−1}(1 − q^{2i}).
items.locator: Definition 2.20 and Remark 2.21, p.14, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.24 (parametrizing lattices over L^♭ and two vanishing sums)
items.statement: For integral L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕): (1) L ↦ (L ∩ V_{L^♭}, δ_L, ε_L) is a bijection from lattices containing L^♭ onto triples (L^{♭′}, δ, ε : u^δ(V^⊥_{L^♭})^int → L^{♭′} ⊗ F/O_F), with an explicit integrality criterion; (2) t(L) = t(L^{♭′}) ± 1 according as im ε ⊆ (u(L^{♭′})^∨ + L^{♭′})/L^{♭′} or not; (3) Σ_{L ⊆ L^∨, L ∩ V_{L^♭} = L^{♭′}} q^{−δ_L}|μ(t(L))| converges, and if t(L^{♭′}) > 1 then Σ_{…, z ∈ L^∨} q^{−δ_L}μ(t(L)) = 0 for every z ∈ 𝐕 \ 𝐕^int; (4) if t(L^{♭′}) > 1, Σ_{…, δ_L = 0} μ(t(L)) = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 2.24 and proof, pp.15–19, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Proposition 2.22 (the analytic vertical part)
items.statement: For L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕), ∂Den^v_{L^♭} extends uniquely to a compactly supported locally constant function on 𝐕 whose Fourier transform is supported in 𝐕^int. (Proved directly, without a functional equation or induction formula; the argument also gives a simpler proof of [LZa, Thm. 7.4.1].)
items.locator: Proposition 2.22, p.15; proof, pp.19–21; §1.2, p.7, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 2.27 (Bruhat–Tits strata V_Λ)
items.statement: For a vertex lattice Λ ⊆ 𝐕, Λ^∨/Λ with (x, y) = u²Tr_{E/F}(x^♯, y^♯)_𝐕 mod u² is a nonsplit nondegenerate quadratic space over k of even dimension t(Λ); V_Λ is the reduced subscheme of N(Λ) and V°_Λ = V_Λ − ⋃_{Λ ⊊ Λ′} V_{Λ′}.
items.locator: Definition 2.27, p.21, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Proposition 2.28 (Bruhat–Tits stratification, Wu)
items.statement: N_red = ⊔_Λ V°_Λ over vertex lattices, with V_Λ ∩ V_{Λ′} = V_{Λ+Λ′} if Λ + Λ′ is vertex and empty otherwise; V_Λ is the generalized Deligne–Lusztig variety of O(Λ^∨/Λ) of maximal isotropic U with dim(U ∩ δ(U)) = t(Λ)/2 − 1; its intersection with each connected component of N_red is connected, nonempty, smooth projective of dimension t(Λ)/2 − 1 [Wu, Prop. 5.13, Thm. 5.18] (for t(Λ) = 4, two copies of P¹, Remark 2.29).
items.locator: Proposition 2.28 and Remark 2.29, pp.21–22 and footnote 8, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: [Wu] treats F = Q_p; footnote 8 asserts the arguments work for general F. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Corollaries 2.30–2.31
items.statement: For 0 ≠ x ∈ 𝐕, N(x)_red = ⋃_{x ∈ Λ} V°_Λ over vertex lattices containing x. If r ≥ 2, N(x) meets each connected component of N_red in a proper closed subscheme (the intersection of all vertex lattices is {0}).
items.locator: Corollaries 2.30–2.31, pp.22–23, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.32 (cycles on V_Λ; Lusztig type ²D)
items.statement: For each connected component V^+_Λ and d ≥ 0, d-cycles on V^+_Λ modulo ℓ-adic homological equivalence (ℓ ≠ p) are generated by the V_{Λ′} ∩ V^+_Λ with Λ′ ⊇ Λ vertex of type 2d + 2. (V^{°+}_Λ is the Coxeter Deligne–Lusztig variety of SO(Λ^∨/Λ) over k′; for t(Λ) ≥ 6, δ² acts semisimply on H_c^* with eigenvalues q^{2j} in degree j + t(Λ)/2 − 1 [Lus76, 7.3 case ²D_n, Thm. 6.1].)
items.locator: Lemma 2.32 and proof, p.23, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Proposition 2.33 and Corollaries 2.34–2.35 (linear invariance)
items.statement: With C(x) = [I_{N(x)} → O_N] (x ≠ 0) and C(0) = [ω →^0 O_N] (2.14): if x_1, …, x_m and y_1, …, y_m generate the same O_E-submodule (0 ≤ m ≤ n), then H^i(C(x_1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ C(x_m)) ≅ H^i(C(y_1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ C(y_m)) for all i (following [How19, Thm. 5.1]); hence the classes agree in K_0(N) [LL21, §B], and the Serre intersection multiplicity of n divisors depends only on the lattice they span.
items.locator: §2.4, (2.14), Proposition 2.33, Corollaries 2.34–2.35, pp.23–24, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: The line bundle of modular forms ω (Lemmas 2.36–2.37, 2.41, Definition 2.38)
items.statement: F_X = ker(ι_X(u) − u | Lie X) is locally free of rank n − 1 and a local direct summand (wedge and spin conditions); F_X^⊥ ⊆ ϵD(X) ⊆ D(X) with ϵ = u ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ u, and ϵ induces a surjection Lie X → ϵD(X)/F_X^⊥ with kernel L_X, a rank-1 local direct summand on which O_E acts via φ_0^c [How19, Prop. 3.3]; L_X is the image of ι_X(u) − u (Lemma 2.41); ω := L_X^{−1}.
items.locator: Lemmas 2.36–2.37, Definition 2.38, Lemma 2.41, pp.24–26, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemmas 2.39–2.40 (N(x) is a relative Cartier divisor)
items.statement: Via Grothendieck–Messing, x extends to x̃ : Fil(X_0)|_{N(x)^≈} → Lie(X)|_{N(x)^≈} on the first-order thickening, and x̃(γ) is a section of L_X whose vanishing locus is N(x) [How19, Prop. 4.1]; hence N(x) is empty or a relative Cartier divisor (r = 1: [RSZ17, Prop. 6.6]; r ≥ 2 via [KR11, Lemma 3.6] and Corollary 2.31).
items.locator: Lemmas 2.39–2.40, p.25, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.42 (degree of ω on Deligne–Lusztig curves)
items.statement: For a vertex lattice Λ with t(Λ) = 4, ω has degree q − 1 on each connected component of the curve V_Λ.
items.locator: Lemma 2.42 and proof, p.26, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Rederived: deg ω^{−1}|_{V^±} = −q·deg(V^±) + (q² + 1) with deg(V^±) = q + 1 in the projective space of lines. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Proposition 2.44 (Theorem 2.7 for r = 1)
items.statement: For an integral O_E-lattice 𝐋 of the nonsplit 2-dimensional 𝐕 with fundamental invariants (2b_1 + 1, 2b_2 + 1): Int(𝐋) = ∂Den(𝐋) = 2Σ_{j=0}^{b_1}(1 + q + ⋯ + q^j + (b_2 − j)q^j). Via N(x_1) = Σ_{j=0}^{b_1} W_{x_1E,j} (quasi-canonical lifting divisors [RSZ17, §6, Prop. 7.1]) and length(W_{x_1E,j} ∩ N(x_2)) = 2(1 + q + ⋯ + q^j + (b_2 − j)q^j) (2.17), by Keating's formula [Vol07, Thm. 2.1] as in [KR11, Prop. 8.4].
items.locator: Proposition 2.44 and proof, pp.27–28, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: (2.17) and the next display print (b_2 − l) for (b_2 − j) (sourceIssues E1). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definition 2.45 and Corollary 2.46 (primitive horizontal divisors, r = 1)
items.statement: N(L^♭)° := N(L^♭) − N(u^{−1}L^♭) (an effective divisor); for x ∈ 𝐕 \ V_{L^♭}, length(N(L^♭)° ∩ N(x)) = 2Σ_{L ⊆ L^∨, L ∩ V_{L^♭} = L^♭} 1_L(x).

items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Definitions 2.47–2.48 and 2.50 (K-classes and horizontal/vertical intersection functions)
items.statement: X^h is cut out by O_X[p^∞]; K_0(X, Z) and F^mK_0(X, Z) are images of K_0^Z(X), F^mK_0^Z(X) in K_0(X) [LL21, §B; Zha21, App. B; GS87]. K_N(X) = [C(x_1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ C(x_m)], K_N(X)^h = [N(X)^h], K_N(X)^v = K_N(X) − K_N(X)^h; for L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕) and x ∈ 𝐕 \ V_{L^♭}: Int_{L^♭}(x) = K_N(L^♭)·K_N(x) = Int(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩), Int^h_{L^♭}(x) = K_N(L^♭)^h·K_N(x), Int^v_{L^♭}(x) = K_N(L^♭)^v·K_N(x).
items.locator: Definitions 2.47–2.48 and 2.50, pp.28–29, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.49
items.statement: For L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕): (1) N(L^♭)^h is empty or finite flat over Spf O_Ĕ; (2) K_N(L^♭), K_N(L^♭)^h, K_N(L^♭)^v ∈ F^{n−1}K_0(N, N(L^♭)); (3) K_N(L^♭)^v lies in Σ_{i=1}^m F^{n−1}K_0(N, V_{Λ_i}) for finitely many vertex lattices Λ_i of type n.
items.locator: Lemma 2.49, pp.28–29, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Remark 2.52 (cancellation law for special cycles)
items.statement: For a nonsplit subspace 𝐕′ of positive even dimension n′ and integral L with L ∩ 𝐕′^⊥ self-dual, there is N′ = N_{(𝐗′)} → N identifying N′ with N(L ∩ 𝐕′^⊥); if L ∩ 𝐕′ ≠ 0 then N(L) is the image of N′(L ∩ 𝐕′); for x = y + x′, N′ ×_N N(x) is ∅, N′ or N′(x′) according as y ∉ L ∩ 𝐕′^⊥, x′ = 0, or otherwise; and Int(L) = Int(L ∩ 𝐕′) for lattices L (as in [LZa, §2.11]; the self-dual lattices here are the u-modular lattices of [RSZ17]).
items.locator: Remark 2.52, pp.29–30, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemmas 2.53–2.54 (the horizontal part)
items.statement: For integral L^{♭′} with t(L^{♭′}) = 1: N(L^{♭′}) is finite flat, and N(L^{♭′})° := N(L^{♭′}) − N(L^{♭′}_−) satisfies N(L^{♭′})°·K_N(x) = 2Σ_{L ⊆ L^∨, L ∩ V_{L^♭} = L^{♭′}} 1_L(x). For L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕): N(L^♭)^h = ⋃_{L^♭ ⊆ L^{♭′} ⊆ (L^{♭′})^∨, t(L^{♭′}) = 1} N(L^{♭′})° and K_N(L^♭)^h = Σ N(L^{♭′})° in F^{n−1}K_0/F^nK_0 (as [LZa, Thm. 4.2.1], with Lemma 2.23(2) replacing [LZa, Lemma 4.5.1]).
items.locator: Lemmas 2.53–2.54, pp.30–31, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.55 (local modularity for a Deligne–Lusztig curve, n = 4)
items.statement: For a vertex lattice Λ with t(Λ) = 4 and a component V^+_Λ: Int_{V^+_Λ}(x) := V^+_Λ·K_N(x) extends to a compactly supported locally constant function equal to −q(1 + q)1_Λ + Σ_{Λ ⊊ Λ′ ⊆ Λ′^∨} 1_{Λ′} (value 1 − q on Λ via the linear-invariance identity O_{N(x)} ⊗^L O_{N(x)} = O_{N(x)} ⊗ C(0) and Lemma 2.42), and (Int_{V^+_Λ})^ = −Int_{V^+_Λ}.
items.locator: Lemma 2.55 and proof, pp.31–32, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The Fourier evaluation (values q − 1, −1, 0, 0 with q² + 1 type-2 lattices over Λ, vol(Λ) = q^{−2}) was rederived. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Lemma 2.56 (the two components contribute equally)
items.statement: Int^+(𝐋) = Int^−(𝐋) = ½Int(𝐋) for the intersection multiplicities on the two connected components N^±: an element θ ∈ U(𝐕)(F) fixing all but one anisotropic vector x_n of a normal basis and negating x_n preserves each N(x_i) and swaps N^+ and N^− (det θ = −1).
items.locator: Lemma 2.56, p.33, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Printed "θ(x_i) = 1" for θ(x_i) = x_i (sourceIssues E2). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B.

items.name: Proposition 2.51 (the geometric side)
items.statement: For L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕): (1) Int^h_{L^♭} = ∂Den^h_{L^♭} on 𝐕 \ V_{L^♭}; (2) Int^v_{L^♭} extends uniquely to a compactly supported locally constant function with (Int^v_{L^♭})^ = −Int^v_{L^♭}, so its Fourier transform is supported in 𝐕^int. (Via Lemmas 2.49(3), 2.32, 2.53–2.55.)
items.locator: Proposition 2.51 and proof, pp.29, 33, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.name: Corollary 2.66, second part (special divisors under −^rel)
items.statement: Under N^Φ ≅ N (Corollary 2.65), N^Φ(x) = N(x^rel) for 0 ≠ x ∈ 𝐕 (parallel to [Mih22, Rem. 4.4]).
items.locator: Corollary 2.66, p.42, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5

items.name: Hermitian O_E-lattices over a ramified extension: normal bases (Definitions 2.10–2.11, Lemma 2.12, Remark 2.13)
items.statement: For L in a hermitian space over ramified E/F: L^∨ = {x : Tr(x, L) ⊆ O_F} = {x : (x, L) ⊆ u^{−1}O_E}; integral, vertex (u kills L^∨/L) and self-dual lattices; fundamental invariants a_i with L^∨/L ≅ ⊕ O_E/(u^{a_i}), type t(L), val(L). A normal basis has moment matrix a permutation of ⊕ β_iu^{2b_i} ⊕ ⊕ [[0, u^{2c_j−1}], [−u^{2c_j−1}, 0]]; normal bases exist, s, t, b_i, c_j are invariants of L [Jac62, Props. 4.3, 8.1, p.449], and the fundamental invariants are the rearrangement of (2b_i + 1, 2c_j, 2c_j). Hence L is vertex iff a_m ≤ 1, self-dual iff a_m = 0, and t(L), val(L) ≡ m mod 2.
items.locator: Definitions 2.10–2.11, Lemma 2.12, Remark 2.13, pp.11–12, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: GN.2 plans local classification of lattices with hermitian variants; the paper derives the rest from Jacobowitz.

items.name: Definition 2.14 (local densities over a ramified extension)
items.statement: Den(M, L) = lim_N #Herm_{L,M}(O_F/(u^{2N}))/q^{N·d_{L,M}}, d_{L,M} = dim Herm_{L,M} ⊗ F; H is the hyperbolic plane with matrix [[0, u^{−1}], [−u^{−1}, 0]] and H_s = H^{⊕s}, self-dual of rank 2s.
items.locator: Definition 2.14, p.12, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.15 (Cho–Yamauchi formula, ramified case)
items.statement: For L of rank m and s ≥ m: Den(H_s, L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} |L′/L|^{m−2s} Π_{s−(m+t(L′))/2 < i ≤ s}(1 − q^{−2i}), over integral lattices of L ⊗ F containing L. (Isometries of the symplectic k-space L′_k, with radical of dimension t(L′), into H_{s,k} number q^{m(4s−m+1)/2}Π_{s−(m+t)/2 < i ≤ s}(1 − q^{−2i}) (2.2).)
items.locator: Lemma 2.15 and proof, pp.12–13, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The count (2.2) was rederived for t = 0, t = m and in general. The summation range is typeset "L′ ⊆ L′vee" (sourceIssues E3). Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Definition 2.16 and Remark 2.17 (normalized local Siegel series, ramified case)
items.statement: For an O_E-lattice 𝐋 of the nonsplit 𝐕 of dimension n = 2r: Den(X, 𝐋) ∈ Z[X] with Den(q^{−s}, 𝐋) = Den(H_{r+s}, 𝐋)/Π_{i=s+1}^{r+s}(1 − q^{−2i}) for s ≥ 0; ∂Den(𝐋) = −(d/dX)|_{X=1} Den(X, 𝐋); Den(1, 𝐋) = Den(H_r, 𝐋) = 0 since 𝐕 is nonsplit.
items.locator: Definition 2.16 and Remark 2.17, p.13, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.19 (weighted lattice counts for Den and ∂Den)
items.locator: Lemma 2.19, p.14, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Rederived from Lemma 2.15 and Definition 2.16. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.23 (invariants from minors; type change)
items.statement: (1) For any basis with moment matrix T, a_1 + ⋯ + a_i − i is the minimal E-valuation of i × i minors of T. (2) If L = L′ + ⟨x⟩ with L′ of rank m − 1, then t(L) = t(L′) + 1 if x′ ∈ uL′^∨ + L′ (x′ ∈ L′^∨ the projection representing (x, −)|_{L′}) and t(L′) − 1 otherwise.
items.locator: Lemma 2.23, p.15, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.25
items.statement: For an integral hermitian O_E-module L of rank 2m + 1 with t(L) = 2m + 1: |(L^∨)^int/L| = q^{2m}|(uL^∨)^int/L| (2.8) (induction on val(L), starting from the q^{2m} isotropic vectors of a (2m + 1)-dimensional quadratic space).
items.locator: Lemma 2.25 and proof, p.19, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.43 (r = 1)
items.statement: For an integral lattice 𝐋 of the nonsplit 2-dimensional 𝐕 with fundamental invariants (2b_1 + 1, 2b_2 + 1): ∂Den(𝐋) = 2Σ_{j=0}^{b_1}(1 + q + ⋯ + q^j + (b_2 − j)q^j), the number of integral overlattices with L ∩ ⟨e_1⟩_F = ⟨u^je_1⟩ being 1 + q + ⋯ + q^j + (b_2 − j)q^j.
items.locator: Lemma 2.43 and proof, p.27, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The overlattice count was rederived. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.57 (special lattices) and the sets S_{L^♭}
items.statement: For r ≥ 2 and integral L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕) with a_{n−2} < a_{n−1}, the number of integral lattices containing L^♭ with fundamental invariants (a_1, …, a_{n−2}, a_{n−1} − 1, a_{n−1} − 1) is 0 or 2; when 2 (L^♭ special), these L^{♭±} satisfy L^{♭±} ∩ V_{L^♭} = L^♭, a_{n−1} ≥ 3, and compatible splittings L^♭ = L^♭_← ⊕ L^♭_→, L^{♭±} = L^♭_← ⊕ L^{♭±}_→. S_{L^♭} = L^{♭+} ∪ L^{♭−} if special and L^♭ + (V^⊥_{L^♭})^int otherwise.
items.locator: Lemma 2.57 and the definition of S_{L^♭}, pp.33–34, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 2.58 (reduction of valuation off S_{L^♭})
items.statement: For integral L^♭ ∈ ♭(𝐕) and x ∈ 𝐕 \ (V_{L^♭} ∪ S_{L^♭}), L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L^{♭′} + ⟨x′⟩ for some L^{♭′} ∈ ♭(𝐕) with val(L^{♭′}) < val(L^♭) (non-integral lattices having val = −1).
items.locator: Lemma 2.58 and proof, p.35, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The proof prints u^{e_i−1} for u^{a_i−1} (sourceIssues E2). Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Fourier transform on hermitian spaces over a ramified extension
items.statement: With ψ_F of conductor O_F: φ̂(x) = ∫_V φ(y)ψ_F(Tr_{E/F}(x, y)_V)dy for the self-dual measure (and on V^r with Σ Tr(x_i, y_i)).
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: The Weil representation of G_r(F) × H_V(F) in the Schrödinger model (ramified case)
items.statement: For the split skew-hermitian W_r = E^{2r} and a split hermitian V of dimension 2r with self-dual Λ_V: ω(m(a))φ(x) = |det a|_E^r φ(xa), ω(n(b))φ(x) = ψ_F(tr bT(x))φ(x), ω(w_r)φ = φ̂, ω(h)φ(x) = φ(h^{−1}x) (trivial splitting character), on C_c^∞(V^r).
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: Definition 3.2, Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.4 (the spherical module)
items.statement: S_{W_r,V} = (K_r × L_V)-fixed vectors of the Weil representation, a module over H_{W_r} ⊗ H_V; 1_{Λ_V^r} ∈ Sph(V^r) (as Λ_V^∨ = Λ_V); and the annihilator of S_{W_r,V} is the diagonal ideal I_{W_r,V} (as in [Liu22, Prop. 4.4] with ε = +, d = r).
items.locator: Definition 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.4, p.44, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.9 (theta lifting of tempered spherical representations)
items.statement: For π = π^σ_{W_r} with σ ∈ (iR/(2πi/log q)Z)^r: θ(π, V) ≅ π^σ_V (Θ(π, V)^{L_V} ≠ 0 as in [Liu22, Thm. 6.2]; Θ(π, V) is semisimple by [GI16, Thm. 4.1(v)]; then Proposition 3.4). [Wal90] gives irreducibility or vanishing of θ(π, V).
items.locator: Proposition 3.9, p.47, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: Remark 3.1 (special maximal compact subgroups for ramified unitary groups)
items.statement: (1) There is κ : W_r → V with (κ(e_i), κ(e_{r+j}))_V = u^{−1}δ_{ij}, the other pairings zero, and L_V the O_E-span of the κ(e_i). (2) K_r\G_r(F)/K_r has representatives diag(u^{a_1}, …, u^{a_r}, (−u)^{−a_1}, …, (−u)^{−a_r}) with 0 ≤ a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_r; both H_{W_r} and H_V are commutative and canonically isomorphic to C[T_1^{±1}, …, T_r^{±1}]^{{±1}^r ⋊ S_r}.
items.locator: Remark 3.1, p.43, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 plans Satake only for unramified groups with hyperspecial level. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Unramified principal series I^σ_{W_r}, I^σ_V and π^σ
items.statement: For σ ∈ (C/(2πi/log q)Z)^r: χ^σ_r(a) = Π|a_i|_E^{σ_i+i−1/2} on the diagonal torus of the Borel P_r (lower-triangular a), I^σ_{W_r} the normalized principal series and π^σ_{W_r} its unique K_r-spherical constituent; likewise χ^σ_V, I^σ_V and π^σ_V for the minimal parabolic Q_V stabilizing the flag spanned by v_r, …, v_i of a basis of Λ_V with (v_i, v_j) = u^{−1}δ_{i,−j}.

items.name: The doubling zeta integral and doubling factors
items.statement: I^□_r(s) = Ind^{G^□_r}_{P^□_r}(|·|_E^s ∘ Δ); f^{(s)}_r is the section with f^{(s)}_r(g) = |Δ(p)|_E^{s+r} for g ∈ pK_r (holomorphic standard, so good), equal to the spherical vector of I^{σ^□_s}_{W_{2r}} with σ^□_s = (s + r − ½, …, s − r + ½) (Remark 3.5); Z(ξ, f(s)) = ∫_{G_r(F)} H_ξ(g)f(s)(w_r(g, 1_{2r}))dg, absolutely convergent for Re s ≫ 0 with meromorphic continuation; L(s, π) and ε(s, π, ψ_F) are the doubling factors of [Yam14, Thm. 5.2].

items.name: Global notation for the doubling method (Notations 4.1–4.3)
items.statement: E/F CM with c; V^spl, V^int, V^ram; b_m(s) = Π_v Π_{i=1}^m L(2s + i, η_v^{m−i}); ψ_T; a totally positive definite hermitian space V over A_E of rank n = 2r with local Hasse invariants ε_v and Diff(T, V); a finite set R ⊇ {v ∈ V^ram: ε_v = −1, v | 2, or v ramified over Q} and S = {v ∉ R : ε_v = −1} ⊆ V^int; the lattice Λ^R with [(Λ^R_v)^∨ : Λ^R_v] = q_v^{1−ε_v}, its stabilizer L^R and Hecke algebras T^R ⊇ S^R; u-nearby spaces ^uV for u ∉ V^spl_E; G_m = U(W_m) with P_m, m(a), n(b), K_m, κ_{m,v}, Haar measures and the spaces A^{[r]R} of automorphic forms.

items.name: Assumptions 1.3 and 4.4 (the representations considered)
items.statement: Assumption 1.3: F ≠ Q, V^spl contains all 2-adic places, every prime in V^ram is unramified over Q; π cuspidal on G_r(A_F) with π_v holomorphic discrete series of Harish-Chandra parameter {(1−n)/2, …, (n−1)/2} at archimedean v, K_{r,v}-spherical at ramified v, unramified or almost unramified at inert v (v unramified over Q if almost unramified), tempered at finite v, and R_π ∪ S_π ⊆ V♥. Assumption 4.4: the corresponding conditions relative to R, with π_v unramified or almost unramified according as ε_v = ±1 off R.

items.name: Definition 4.6, Remark 4.7 and Proposition 4.8 (L-function and local theta dichotomy)

For every finite v, dim Hom(I^□_{r,v}(0), π_v ⊠ π_v^∨) = 1; for v ∈ (V^fin \ R) ∪ V^spl, V_v is the unique hermitian space with ℨ^♮_{π_v,V_v} ≠ 0; Hom_{G_r(F_v)}(S(V_v^r), π_v) is irreducible and nonzero for such v.

items.name: Kudla's special cycles and generating functions in Chow groups
items.statement: For the unitary Shimura variety X_L of dimension n − 1 over E (complex uniformization by ^uH(F)\𝔇 × H(A_F)/L, Deligne homomorphism of [LTXZZ, §3.2]), Z_T(φ^∞)_L = Σ_{x ∈ L\V^m ⊗ A^∞_F, T(x) = T} φ^∞(x)Z(x)_L ∈ CH^m(X_L)_C with Z(x)_L Kudla's special cycle [LL21, Def. 4.1], and Z_{φ^∞}(g)_L = Σ_{T ∈ Herm_m(F)^+} ω_{m,∞}(g_∞)φ^0_∞(T)·Z_T(ω^∞_m(g^∞)φ^∞)_L.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Hypothesis 4.11 (modularity of generating functions), assumed
items.statement: For every L, φ^∞ and linear l : CH^m(X_L)_C → C, g ↦ l(Z_{φ^∞}(g)_L) converges absolutely and lies in A^{[r]}(G_m(F)\G_m(A_F)) [LL21, Hyp. 4.5].
items.locator: Hypothesis 4.11, pp.53–54, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: A hypothesis of Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.7; Theorem 1.4 does not use it. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definition 4.12 (arithmetic theta lifting)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 4.11, for φ ∈ V_π^{[r]} and φ^∞: Θ_{φ^∞}(φ)_L = ∫_{G_r(F)\G_r(A_F)} φ^c(g)Z_{φ^∞}(g)_L dg ∈ CH^r(X_L)_C [LL21, Prop. 4.7], with image Θ_{φ^∞}(φ) in CH^r(X)_C = colim_L CH^r(X_L)_C; Θ(π, V) is the span of all Θ_{φ^∞}(φ).
items.locator: Definition 4.12, p.54, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Beilinson's height pairing and local indices (ℓ-adic version)
items.statement: For ℓ with X_{L,u} of smooth projective reduction at all u | ℓ: ⟨ , ⟩^ℓ_{X_L,E} on CH^r(X_L)_C^{⟨ℓ⟩}, complex-linear in the first variable and conjugate symmetric, with ⟨c_1, c_2⟩^ℓ = Σ_{u|∞} 2⟨c_1, c_2⟩_{X_L,u,E_u} + Σ_{u finite} log q_u·⟨c_1, c_2⟩^ℓ_{X_L,u,E_u} for disjointly supported cycles (non-archimedean local indices [LL21, §B], archimedean [LL21, §10]).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definitions 4.13–4.15 (R-good primes, Hecke subalgebras, admissible sextuples, global and local indices)
items.statement: ℓ is R-good if unramified in E with V_F^(ℓ) ⊆ V^fin \ (R ∪ S). (S^R_𝕃)^0_{L_R} annihilates H^i_dR (i ≠ 2r − 1) and (S^R_𝕃)^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R} annihilates ⊕_{u ∤ ℓ} H^{2r}(X_{L_RL^R,u}, Q_ℓ(r)). An (R, R′, ℓ, L)-admissible sextuple (φ^∞_1, φ^∞_2, s_1, s_2, g_1, g_2) has φ^∞_{iv} = 1_{(Λ^R_v)^r} off R, regular support at v ∈ R′, s_i products of two elements of (S^R_{Q^ac})^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R}, g_i ∈ G_r(A^{R′}_F); the global index I_{T_1,T_2}(…)^ℓ_L pairs the weighted cycles s_i^*Z_{T_i}(…) and the local indices I_{T_1,T_2}(…)_{L,u} are its u-components.
items.locator: Definitions 4.13–4.15, pp.54–55, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Remark 4.16 and Definition 4.17 (normalized height pairing)
items.statement: For L = L_RL^R: s^*Θ_{φ^∞}(φ)_L = χ^R_π(s)^cΘ_{φ^∞}(φ)_L for s ∈ S^R_{Q^ac}, Θ_{φ^∞}(φ)_L ∈ CH^r(X_L)^0_C, and under [LL21, Hyp. 6.6] Θ_{φ^∞}(φ)_L ∈ CH^r(X_L)^{⟨ℓ⟩}_C for R-good ℓ [LL21, Prop. 6.10]. Under [LL21, Hyp. 6.6], ⟨Θ_{φ^∞_1}(φ_1), Θ_{φ^∞_2}(φ_2)⟩^♮_{X,E} := vol^♮(L)·⟨Θ_{φ^∞_1}(φ_1)_L, Θ_{φ^∞_2}(φ_2)_L⟩^ℓ_{X_L,E}, independent of L.
items.locator: Remark 4.16 and Definition 4.17, pp.55–56, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.20 (local indices at split places vanish)
items.statement: For |R′| ≥ 2 and u ∈ V^spl_E with u ∉ R \ V♥ and V_F^(p) ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F, there are s^u_1, s^u_2 ∈ S^R_{Q^ac} \ 𝔪^R_π with I_{T_1,T_2}(φ^∞_1, φ^∞_2, s^u_1s_1, s^u_2s_2, g_1, g_2)^ℓ_{L,u} = 0 for every admissible sextuple and all (T_1, T_2) ∈ Herm°_r(F)^+ (s^u_i = 1 if u ∉ R); this is [LL21, Prop. 7.1] without its restriction on π_u and without [LL21, Hyp. 6.6], using Theorem 4.21.
items.locator: Proposition 4.20, p.57, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.27 (local indices at inert places)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^int_E with p odd and V_F^(p) ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F: (1) if u ∉ S, log q_u·vol^♮(L)·I_{T_1,T_2}(…)^ℓ_{L,u} = 𝔈_{T_1,T_2}((g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (s_1φ^∞_1 ⊗ (s_2φ^∞_2)^c))_u; (2) if u ∈ S ∩ V♥ is unramified over Q, after multiplying by suitable s^u_i ∉ 𝔪^R_π the same holds up to the correction −(log q_u/(q_u^r − 1))E_{T_1,T_2}((g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (…)^{∞,u} ⊗ 1_{(Λ^★_u)^{2r}}) (as [LL21, Props. 8.1, 9.1]).
items.locator: Proposition 4.27, p.64, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.30, second part (special cycles under uniformization)
items.statement: For p-basic φ^∞ [LL21, Def. 6.5] and totally positive t ∈ F: Υ^rel(Z_t(φ^∞)_L̃|_{X^∧_0}) = Σ_{x ∈ U(𝐕)(F)\𝐕, (x,x)_𝐕 = t} Σ_{h ∈ U(𝐕_x)(F)\U(𝐕)(A^{∞,u}_F)/Π 𝐋_v} 𝛟(h^{−1}x)·(N(x^rel), h) (4.9), with 𝛟_v = φ^∞_v off V_F^(p) \ V^spl and 1_{𝚲_v} at v ∈ U (as [Liu21, Thm. 5.22], then Corollary 2.66).
items.locator: Proposition 4.30, (4.9), p.67, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.28 (local indices at ramified places)
items.statement: For u ∈ V^ram_E with V_F^(p) ∩ R ⊆ V^spl_F: log q_u·vol^♮(L)·I_{T_1,T_2}(…)^ℓ_{L,u} = 𝔈_{T_1,T_2}((g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (s_1φ^∞_1 ⊗ (s_2φ^∞_2)^c))_u. Proof: the models X_L̃, Proposition 4.30, and χ(O_{N(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{N(x_{2r})}) = (b_{2r,u}(0)/log q_u)W′_{T^□}(0, 1_{4r}, 1_{(Λ^R_u)^{2r}}) by Theorem 2.7, Remark 2.18 and b_{2r,u}(0) = Π_{i=1}^r (1 − q_u^{−2i}).
items.locator: Proposition 4.28 and proof, pp.64–65, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Proposition 4.31 (local indices at archimedean places)
items.statement: For u ∈ V_E^(∞), an admissible sextuple, φ_1 ∈ V_π^{[r]R}, K_1 fixing φ^∞_1 and φ_1, and a Siegel fundamental domain 𝔉_1: vol^♮(L)·∫_{𝔉_1} φ^c(τ_1g_1)Σ_{T_1} I_{T_1,T_2}(…, τ_1g_1, g_2)_{L,u}dτ_1 = ½∫_{𝔉_1} φ^c(τ_1g_1)Σ_{T_1} 𝔈_{T_1,T_2}((τ_1g_1, g_2), Φ^0_∞ ⊗ (…))_u dτ_1, both absolutely convergent [LL21, Prop. 10.1].
items.locator: Proposition 4.31, p.68, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (nonvanishing of Chow groups)
items.statement: Let (π, V_π) satisfy Assumption 1.3 with r[F:Q] + |S_π| odd and assume [LL21, Hyp. 6.6]. If L′(½, π) ≠ 0 (ord_{s=1/2} L(s, π) = 1), then for every R ⊇ R_π with |R ∩ V^spl ∩ V♥| ≥ 2: colim_{L_R} (CH^r(X_{L_RL^R})^0_{Q^ac})_{𝔪^R_π} ≠ 0.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p.4; proof §4.7, p.68, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Remark 1.9/4.32: [LL21, Hyp. 6.6] is not needed when S_π = ∅. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 1.5 (arithmetic inner product formula)
items.statement: Under Assumption 1.3 with r[F:Q] + |S_π| odd, [LL21, Hyp. 6.6] and Hypothesis 4.11 in codimension r: (1) for φ_i = ⊗φ_{iv} ∈ V_π with lowest-weight archimedean components and ⟨φ^c_{1v}, φ_{2v}⟩ = 1 there, and φ^∞_i ∈ S(V^r ⊗ A^∞_F): ⟨Θ_{φ^∞_1}(φ_1), Θ_{φ^∞_2}(φ_2)⟩^♮_{X,E} = (L′(½, π)/b_{2r}(0))·C_r^{[F:Q]}·Π_{v finite} ℨ^♮_{π_v,V_v}(φ^c_{1v}, φ_{2v}, φ^∞_{1v} ⊗ (φ^∞_{2v})^c) [Liu11a, Conj. 3.11]; (2) if L′(½, π) ≠ 0 then Hom_{H(A^∞_F)}(π̃^∞, colim_L CH^r(X_L)^0_C) ≠ 0, π̃^∞ the theta lift of π^∞.
items.locator: Theorem 1.5 and Remark 1.6, pp.4–5, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The height lies a priori in C ⊗ Q_ℓ; the identity implies it is in C and independent of ℓ (footnote 3). Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 1.7 (explicit height formula for new vectors)
items.statement: In Theorem 1.5(1) with R_π = ∅, φ_1 = φ_2 = φ ∈ V_π^{[r]∅} (holomorphic new forms) normalized everywhere and φ^∞_v = 1_{(Λ^∅_v)^r}: ⟨Θ_{φ^∞}(φ), Θ_{φ^∞}(φ)⟩^♮_{X,E} = (−1)^r·(L′(½, π)/b_{2r}(0))·|C_r|^{[F:Q]}·Π_{v∈S_π} q_v^{r−1}(q_v + 1)/((q_v^{2r−1} + 1)(q_v^{2r} − 1)). (Remark 1.8: with injectivity of the étale Abel–Jacobi map and Beilinson's positivity conjecture this is equivalent to L′(½, π) ≥ 0.)
items.locator: Corollary 1.7 and Remark 1.8, pp.5–6, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The sign (−1)^r was checked against Proposition 4.9 and the parity of r[F:Q] + |S_π|. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Example 1.10 (symmetric powers of elliptic curves)
items.statement: For r ≥ 2 and a non-CM elliptic curve A/F with Sym^{2r−1}A (hence Sym^{2r−1}A_E) modular, with Π the cuspidal representation of GL_n(A_E) (Π^∨ ≅ Π ∘ c): a π as in Assumption 1.3 with base change Π exists iff A has good reduction at every v ∈ V^fin \ V^spl; then S_π = ∅ and ε(π) = (−1)^{r[F:Q]}, so the results apply when r and [F:Q] are odd.
items.locator: Example 1.10 and footnote 4, p.6, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Stated without proof. Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Remarks 4.32–4.33 (removing Hypothesis 6.6; the case F = Q)
items.statement: When S_π = ∅, Theorems 1.4, 1.5 and Corollary 1.7 hold without [LL21, Hyp. 6.6], by redefining (S^R_𝕃)^{⟨ℓ⟩}_{L_R} via the cycle-class image H^{2r}_† and using Theorem 4.21 (H^{2r}_† is a quotient of H^{2r}(X_m, Q_ℓ(r))). For F = Q and r ≥ 2 the obstacle is compactifying integral models with Drinfeld level at split places together with a vanishing theorem like 4.21.
items.locator: Remarks 4.32–4.33, pp.68–69, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryArithmeticInnerProductFormula (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Newton strata of Y_m and the strata Y^(M)_m
items.statement: Y_m = X_m ⊗ k; h(x) ∈ [0, n − 1] is the étale height of the 1-dimensional O_{F_u}-divisible group A_x[u^{c,∞}] of height n; Y^[h]_m (h(x) ≤ h, reduced, closed) and Y^(h)_m = Y^[h]_m − Y^[h−1]_m, smooth of pure dimension h. For m ≥ 1, 𝔖^h_m = free rank-(n − h) O_{F_u}/𝔭^m-submodules of (𝔭^{−m}/O)^n, Y^(M)_m the locus where the Drinfeld structure has kernel M, and Y^[M]_m = ⊔_{M ⊆ M′} Y^(M′)_m (4.1), preserved by Hecke operators away from u.
items.locator: §4.3, pp.58, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 4.22–4.23 (counting parabolic cosets and fixed vectors)
items.statement: C^{g_1,…,g_t}_m = #GL_g(O/𝔭^m)/P_{g_1,…,g_t}(O/𝔭^m) satisfies C^{g′−g,g}_m C^{g_1,…,g_t}_m = C^{g′−g+g_1,g_2,…,g_t}_m; and dim(Ind_{P_{g_1,…,g_t}}^{GL_g} π_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ π_t)^{L^g_{u,m}} = C^{g_1,…,g_t}_m Π_i dim π_i^{L^{g_i}_{u,m}} for m ≥ 1.
items.locator: Lemmas 4.22–4.23, pp.58–59, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.24 (alternating sum over Steinberg representations)
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, g ≥ 1 and an unramified character φ of F_u^×: Σ_{h=0}^{g} (−1)^h C^{g−h,h}_m dim Sp_h(φ)^{L^h_{u,m}} = 0, from Σ_h (−1)^h[Ind_{P_{h,g−h}} Sp_h(φ) ⊠ φ|·|^{(g+h−1)/2} ∘ det] = 0 in Groth(GL_g(F_u)) [Zel80; HT01, Lemma I.3.2].
items.locator: Lemma 4.24 and proof, pp.59–60, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: The telescoping identity was checked. The proof writes σ(i) for σ(h) (sourceIssues E3). Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

items.name: Smoothness of closures of refined Newton strata (Mantovan)
items.statement: Each Y^[M]_m is smooth over k of pure dimension h [Man08, Prop. 12], and Y^(M)_m ≅ the Igusa variety of the first kind I^h_m [HT01, §IV.1] as k-schemes.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 4.25 and Theorem 4.21, pp.60, 62–63, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

items.name: The Igusa trace formula with endoscopy (Caraiani–Scholze)
items.statement: [H_{c,χ}(I^{h′}_m, Q_ℓ)] = Σ_𝐧 Σ_{Π_𝐧} c(𝐧, Π_𝐧)·Red^{h′}_𝐧(π^𝐧_u)^{O^×_{D_{n−h′}} × L^{h′}_{u,m}} (4.4) in Groth(D^×_{n−h′}/O^×), over elliptic endoscopic groups G_𝐧 (𝐧 = (n_1, n_2)), cohomological isobaric Π_𝐧, with Red^{h′}_𝐧 the composite of Jacquet functor, parabolic induction and the Langlands–Jacquet map [CS17, Lemma 5.5.1].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.25, (4.4), pp.60–61, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: IG.5 plans the rational Igusa trace comparison computing the alternating Q_ℓ-representation of Igusa cohomology.

items.name: Deligne's purity for proper smooth varieties over finite fields
items.statement: For Y proper smooth over a finite field, H^j(Y_k̄, Q_ℓ) is pure of weight j; used to deduce vanishing from strict purity of weight h.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 4.25 and Theorem 4.21, pp.62–63, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: R34.5 plans Weil I and the required Weil II purity statements.

items.name: Proposition 4.25 (localized cohomology of closed Newton strata)
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, 0 ≤ h ≤ n − 1 and M ∈ 𝔖^h_m: H^j(Y^[M]_m ⊗ F̄_p, Q_ℓ)_𝔪 = 0 for j ≠ h (extending [TY07, Prop. 4.4] to arbitrary principal level at u and to endoscopy): by (4.3)–(4.7) and Lemma 4.24, [H_χ(Y^[M]_m)]_𝔪 is strictly pure of weight h; Y^[M]_m is proper smooth.
items.locator: Proposition 4.25 and proof, pp.60–62, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.21 (vanishing of localized middle cohomology)
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 4.20 with u ∈ V♥ and p ≠ ℓ, for every m ≥ 0: (H^{2r}(X_m, Q_ℓ(r)) ⊗ Q^ac)_𝔪 = 0, where 𝔪 = 𝔪^R_π ∩ S^{R ∪ V_F^(p)}_{Q^ac} (confirming [LL21, Rem. 7.4]). Via proper base change to Y_m, the claim H^j_c(Y^(Σ)_m)_𝔪 = H^j(Y^[Σ]_m)_𝔪 = 0 for j > h (induction on h), and H^1(k, H^h_c(Y^(M)_m)(r))_𝔪 = 0. Remark 4.26: for general n, (H^{n′}(X_m, Q_ℓ(r′)) ⊗ Q^ac)_𝔪 = 0 for n ≤ n′ ≤ 2r′.
items.locator: Theorem 4.21, p.58; proof pp.62–63; Remark 4.26, p.63, Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022), e5
items.note: Routed to IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.5/IG.7 as a source.

routes.reason: The ramified Kudla–Rapoport-type formula, its analytic and geometric sides, the orthogonal Deligne–Lusztig strata and the linear-invariance method are the ramified continuation of the local Kudla–Rapoport theory proposed as UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles. No atlas stage plans them.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: the arithmetic inner product formula for unitary groups
routes.reason: GZ plans rank-one height formulas (point heights, Waldspurger theta kernels, and generating series against incoherent kernels on Shimura curves) but no Beilinson–Bloch heights of arithmetic theta lifts on higher unitary Shimura varieties, no doubling method at ramified places, and no local-index decomposition of the arithmetic inner product formula. These extend GZ's arithmetic-heights direction and consume the two unitary Part IIs rather than duplicating them.
